newsitem.title: SPAIN: Analysts herald Telefonica alliance as bold move.
newsitem.headline: Analysts herald Telefonica alliance as bold move.

text.p: Telefonica de Espana's global alliance with BT and MCI is a bold move that seals its pan-American network and strengthens its position in the key Latin America market, analysts said on Friday.
Telefonica announced it had formed a global telecoms alliance with British Telecommunications and U.S. group MCI Communications Corp, to create one of the world's top five telecoms operators.

"This is a good deal for Telefonica as it has got what it wanted: retaining control of its Latin American interests and getting much-needed money to finance investments," said Javier Borrachero, telecoms analyst at Banco Central Hispano (BCH).
Analysts cheered the global alliance which they said would force Telefonica to abandon its flagging Unisource alliance with U.S. group AT&T Corp.
"The Unisource consortium was not very aggressive in its investment policy whereas BT and MCI are very aggressive and they are moving fast in Europe and Asia," said Borrachero.
But some were slightly unnerved by how the flagship Spanish telecoms carrier would remove itself from the alliance.
"There will be a period of time before the Unisource issue is resolved as the partnership could take Telefonica to court over this," said James Downie, telecoms analyst at ABN-Amro.
"It will be interesting to know how Telefonica will be compensated for the sale of its stake in that business."
Telefonica said in a note to analysts that the BT/MCI global alliance did not contravene its commitments to the Unisource alliance, but that it contacted its partners to reconsider its position.
Analysts said they had been pleasantly surprised by an agreement between BT and Telefonica to exchange shares.

Telefonica said it would take a one percent stake in BT, while the British company will buy a two percent stake in Telefonica. The crossholdings will cost around 280 million pounds ($457.2 million), BT said.
"It's interesting to note that there's been a crossholding as it was not fully expected, but it helps seal the deal," said Downie.
But analysts were eager to know the details of how Telefonica would integrate into BT's European strategy. Its strategy had previously been dictated through its Unisource alliance.
"Before I revise my outlook I want to clarify how Telefonica's strategy in Europe is going to work with BT," said an analyst at a Spanish bank who declined to be named.
By joining with BT, analysts said Telefonica had assured itself of greater access to funding to finance further deals in the burgeoning Latin American market, especially in Brasil.
"The alliance also rids Telefonica of one of its most feared competitors (BT)," said one analyst.
Through MCI, Telefonica will be thrust back into the Mexican market and has also secured a position in the Hispanic market in the United States, analysts said.
"The Mexico market is an important market worth some $7 billion which is expected to double in the next five years," said Downie.
The agreement will allow Telefonica to keep control of its stakes and management in South American operators, an important success for the Spanish company, analysts said.
"AT&T wanted to keep control of the local operators but this was contrary to Telefonica's strategy," said Borrachero.
The deal to join BT's Concert alliance had been widely expected. The alliance's newest partner Portugal Telecom had let slip in its own announcement a reference to Telefonica joining up with MCI.
The news sent Telefonica down 10 pesetas to 3,560 pesetas at the open. But by 1100 GMT, the shares were unchanged at 3,565.
"This news had already largely been discounted by the market, but in the long run will be positive," said one dealer.
